(10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. (18) Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by assistants/paralegals, Professional personnel in accordance with their profession in the form of psychologists and social workers, including advocates for the empowerment and recovery of Victims of Violence. (19) Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. (20) Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. (21) Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to family, substitute family, or community or other social institutions that can provide social support and prevention efforts. (22) Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. (23) Recovery in the broad sense, hereinafter abbreviated as PDML, is a process of supporting women and child victims of violence to become empowered to make decisions and pursue a just, dignified, and prosperous life, through a victim-centered approach, rights-based, multidimensional, community-based, and sustainable, continuous, and participatory in nature, carried out by the regional government involving the role of family and community. (24) Institution for the administration of protection of women and children (hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA) is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively, with quality, including complaint and information services, assistance and legal aid, PDML (recovery in the broad sense) services, consisting of counseling, psychosocial, fulfillment of economic, social and cultural rights, medical services, and safe houses through a referral mechanism; (25) Counseling is an effort to help and or assist victims in interpreting the facts related to choices, plans, or adjustments that need to be made in the psychological development of victims carried out by psychologists or psychiatrists. (26) Psychosocial is a victim recovery mechanism that integrates social support in the community and fulfillment of victims' rights by the government including opening access and information for victims. (27) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection. (28) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(29) Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional government to provide services to Women and Child victims of violence comprehensively and with quality including Information services related to victims' rights, Service for Handling complaints of victims of violence against women and children, Health Services for women and child victims of violence, Psychosocial Services for women and child victims of violence, legal assistance services and repatriation and Social Reintegration services as well as safe house services through a referral mechanism. (30) Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the Administration of Prevention and Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence. (31) Safe House is temporary housing provided to provide Protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards. (32) Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. (33) Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman. (34) Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. (35) Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman and/or Child. a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. justice and gender equality; d. the best interests of the Child; e. respect for the opinions of Women and Children; and f. justice and protection for women and child Victims of Violence. g. The right of children to life, survival, and development. c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence. g. empowerment of Victims and their families.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

(8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

(29) Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional government to provide services to Women and Child victims of violence comprehensively and with quality including Information services related to victims' rights, Service for Handling complaints of victims of violence against women and children, Health Services for women and child victims of violence, Psychosocial Services for women and child victims of violence, legal assistance services and repatriation and Social Reintegration services as well as safe house services through a referral mechanism. (30) Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the Administration of Prevention and Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence. (31) Safe House is temporary housing provided to provide Protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards. (32) Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. (33) Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman. (34) Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. (35) Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman and/or Child. (36) Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. (37) The Administration of Protection of Women and Children is based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. justice and gender equality; d. the best interests of the Child; e. respect for the opinions of Women and Children; and f. justice and protection for women and child Victims of Violence. g. The right of children to life, survival, and development. (38) The Administration of Protection of Women and Children aims to: a. provide Services and Protection to Women and child victims of violence based on gender-based violence and the best interests of children that occur in the home and in society (public); b. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence. (39) The scope of Protection of Women and Children includes: a. institutional matters; b. forms and mechanisms of handling; c. prevention of acts of violence against women and children; d. assistance mechanisms; e. services for Victims of Violence; f. recovery of victims of violence; and
g. empowerment of Victims and their families.

Article 1

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

(29) Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional government to provide services to Women and Child victims of violence comprehensively and with quality including Information services related to victims' rights, Service for Handling complaints of victims of violence against women and children, Health Services for women and child victims of violence, Psychosocial Services for women and child victims of violence, legal assistance services and repatriation and Social Reintegration services as well as safe house services through a referral mechanism. (30) Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the Administration of Prevention and Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence. (31) Safe House is temporary housing provided to provide Protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards. (32) Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. (33) Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman. (34) Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. (35) Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman and/or Child. (36) Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. (37) The Administration of Protection of Women and Children is based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. justice and gender equality; d. the best interests of the Child; e. respect for the opinions of Women and Children; and f. justice and protection for women and child Victims of Violence. g. The right of children to life, survival, and development. (38) The Administration of Protection of Women and Children aims to: a. provide Services and Protection to Women and child victims of violence based on gender-based violence and the best interests of children that occur in the home and in society (public); b. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children; and
c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence. (39) The scope of Protection of Women and Children includes: a. institutional matters; b. forms and mechanisms of handling; c. prevention of acts of violence against women and children; d. assistance mechanisms; e. services for Victims of Violence; f. recovery of victims of violence; and
g. empowerment of Victims and their families.

(7) Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur or has occurred. (8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

Article 1

(7) Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur or has occurred. (8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. (17) Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals. (18) Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by assistants/paralegals, Professional personnel in accordance with their profession in the form of psychologists and social workers, including advocates for the empowerment and recovery of Victims of Violence. (19) Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. (20) Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. (21) Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to family, substitute family, or community or other social institutions that can provide social support and prevention efforts. (22) Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. (23) Recovery in the broad sense, hereinafter abbreviated as PDML, is a process of supporting women and child victims of violence to become empowered to make decisions and pursue a just, dignified, and prosperous life, through a victim-centered approach, rights-based, multidimensional, community-based, and sustainable, continuous, and participatory in nature, carried out by the regional government involving the role of family and community. (24) Institution for the administration of protection of women and children (hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA) is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively, with quality, including complaint and information services, assistance and legal aid, PDML (recovery in the broad sense) services, consisting of counseling, psychosocial, fulfillment of economic, social and cultural rights, medical services, and safe houses through a referral mechanism; (25) Counseling is an effort to help and or assist victims in interpreting the facts related to choices, plans, or adjustments that need to be made in the psychological development of victims carried out by psychologists or psychiatrists. (26) Psychosocial is a victim recovery mechanism that integrates social support in the community and fulfillment of victims' rights by the government including opening access and information for victims. (27) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection. (28) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

CONCERNING

FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

(1) Region is West Seram Regency. (2) Regional Government is the Administration of Government Affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives. (3) Regent is the Regent of West Seram. (4) Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of West Seram Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. (5) Administration is the form of implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence. (6) Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. (7) Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur or has occurred. (8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. (17) Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals. (18) Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by assistants/paralegals, Professional personnel in accordance with their profession in the form of psychologists and social workers, including advocates for the empowerment and recovery of Victims of Violence. (19) Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. (20) Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. (21) Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to family, substitute family, or community or other social institutions that can provide social support and prevention efforts. (22) Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. (23) Recovery in the broad sense, hereinafter abbreviated as PDML, is a process of supporting women and child victims of violence to become empowered to make decisions and pursue a just, dignified, and prosperous life, through a victim-centered approach, rights-based, multidimensional, community-based, and sustainable, continuous, and participatory in nature, carried out by the regional government involving the role of family and community. (24) Institution for the administration of protection of women and children (hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA) is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively, with quality, including complaint and information services, assistance and legal aid, PDML (recovery in the broad sense) services, consisting of counseling, psychosocial, fulfillment of economic, social and cultural rights, medical services, and safe houses through a referral mechanism; (25) Counseling is an effort to help and or assist victims in interpreting the facts related to choices, plans, or adjustments that need to be made in the psychological development of victims carried out by psychologists or psychiatrists. (26) Psychosocial is a victim recovery mechanism that integrates social support in the community and fulfillment of victims' rights by the government including opening access and information for victims. (27) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection. (28) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

(1) Region is West Seram Regency. (2) Regional Government is the Administration of Government Affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives. (3) Regent is the Regent of West Seram. (4) Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of West Seram Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. (5) Administration is the form of implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence. (6) Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. (7) Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur or has occurred. (8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. (17) Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals. (18) Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by assistants/paralegals, Professional personnel in accordance with their profession in the form of psychologists and social workers, including advocates for the empowerment and recovery of Victims of Violence. (19) Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. (20) Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. (21) Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to family, substitute family, or community or other social institutions that can provide social support and prevention efforts. (22) Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. (23) Recovery in the broad sense, hereinafter abbreviated as PDML, is a process of supporting women and child victims of violence to become empowered to make decisions and pursue a just, dignified, and prosperous life, through a victim-centered approach, rights-based, multidimensional, community-based, and sustainable, continuous, and participatory in nature, carried out by the regional government involving the role of family and community. (24) Institution for the administration of protection of women and children (hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA) is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively, with quality, including complaint and information services, assistance and legal aid, PDML (recovery in the broad sense) services, consisting of counseling, psychosocial, fulfillment of economic, social and cultural rights, medical services, and safe houses through a referral mechanism; (25) Counseling is an effort to help and or assist victims in interpreting the facts related to choices, plans, or adjustments that need to be made in the psychological development of victims carried out by psychologists or psychiatrists. (26) Psychosocial is a victim recovery mechanism that integrates social support in the community and fulfillment of victims' rights by the government including opening access and information for victims. (27) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection. (28) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

(1) Region is West Seram Regency. (2) Regional Government is the Administration of Government Affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives. (3) Regent is the Regent of West Seram. (4) Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of West Seram Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. (5) Administration is the form of implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence. (6) Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. (7) Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur or has occurred. (8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. (17) Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals. (18) Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by assistants/paralegals, Professional personnel in accordance with their profession in the form of psychologists and social workers, including advocates for the empowerment and recovery of Victims of Violence. (19) Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. (20) Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. (21) Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to family, substitute family, or community or other social institutions that can provide social support and prevention efforts. (22) Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. (23) Recovery in the broad sense, hereinafter abbreviated as PDML, is a process of supporting women and child victims of violence to become empowered to make decisions and pursue a just, dignified, and prosperous life, through a victim-centered approach, rights-based, multidimensional, community-based, and sustainable, continuous, and participatory in nature, carried out by the regional government involving the role of family and community. (24) Institution for the administration of protection of women and children (hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA) is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively, with quality, including complaint and information services, assistance and legal aid, PDML (recovery in the broad sense) services, consisting of counseling, psychosocial, fulfillment of economic, social and cultural rights, medical services, and safe houses through a referral mechanism; (25) Counseling is an effort to help and or assist victims in interpreting the facts related to choices, plans, or adjustments that need to be made in the psychological development of victims carried out by psychologists or psychiatrists. (26) Psychosocial is a victim recovery mechanism that integrates social support in the community and fulfillment of victims' rights by the government including opening access and information for victims. (27) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection. (28) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

FOR WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act toward a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and demeans the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Child Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore the implementation is needed

of comprehensive Protection for Women and Children.

In order to prevent and address Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that demeans human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates Protection efforts for Women and Children, particularly in terms of institutions, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, assistance mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 7

(1) The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out in an integrated manner through P2TP2A.

(2) The establishment of P2TP2A. as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent Decree.

(3) Further provisions regarding the position, duties, functions and working procedures of P2TP2A. as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children.

(2) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted through: a. Notification of job opportunity information for Women Victims of Violence;

b. education and training for Women Victims of Violence; c. educational assistance for Women and Child Victims of Violence who are withdrawn from education; and

d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of Women Victims of Violence.

(3) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be implemented in the form of agreements.

Article 10

Letter a

What is meant by "medical services" is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims conducted by medical personnel and paramedics

Letter b

What is meant by "medicolegal services" is a form of medical service for the purpose of evidence in the legal field. Letter c What is meant by "psychosocial services" is services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation and to provide social support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving their problems.

Letter d

What is meant by "legal services" is services to assist victims in undergoing the legal process. Letter e What is meant by "economic independence services" is services conducted through skills training and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Part Four

Assistance Mechanisms

Article 14

(1) Assistance is carried out by individuals or persons and/or institutions in cooperation with P2TP2A and building case referral mechanisms.

(2) The assistance mechanism as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOP).

(3) Further provisions regarding the assistance mechanism as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

(1) Region is West Seram Regency. (2) Regional Government is the Administration of Government Affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives. (3) Regent is the Regent of West Seram. (4) Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of West Seram Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. (5) Administration is the form of implementation of Protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence. (6) Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecution, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. (7) Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will occur or has occurred. (8) Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. (9) Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. (10) Violence against Women is any act based on gender distinction that results or may result in suffering or harm to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. (11) Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child. (12) Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. (13) Sexual Violence is any act that violates a person's human dignity based on gender discrimination, which targets a person's body and sexuality that results or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political, and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. (14) Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance. (15) Psychological Violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. (16) Victim is Women and Children, as well as vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities, who experience acts of Violence. (17) Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals. (18) Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by assistants/paralegals, Professional personnel in accordance with their profession in the form of psychologists and social workers, including advocates for the empowerment and recovery of Victims of Violence. (19) Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. (20) Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. (21) Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to family, substitute family, or community or other social institutions that can provide social support and prevention efforts. (22) Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. (23) Recovery in the broad sense, hereinafter abbreviated as PDML, is a process of supporting women and child victims of violence to become empowered to make decisions and pursue a just, dignified, and prosperous life, through a victim-centered approach, rights-based, multidimensional, community-based, and sustainable, continuous, and participatory in nature, carried out by the regional government involving the role of family and community. (24) Institution for the administration of protection of women and children (hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA) is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively, with quality, including complaint and information services, assistance and legal aid, PDML (recovery in the broad sense) services, consisting of counseling, psychosocial, fulfillment of economic, social and cultural rights, medical services, and safe houses through a referral mechanism; (25) Counseling is an effort to help and or assist victims in interpreting the facts related to choices, plans, or adjustments that need to be made in the psychological development of victims carried out by psychologists or psychiatrists. (26) Psychosocial is a victim recovery mechanism that integrates social support in the community and fulfillment of victims' rights by the government including opening access and information for victims. (27) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection. (28) Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
